_note: Foundational text (Kevin, 2026-11-23): the sub-kind 'text' of society, in pipelines/common/event_categories.py (VOCAB 'society', TEXT_ID, the INFOBOX and CATEGORY rules). The class is Wikidata's 'foundational text' (Q3519366). Each family below is a kind of text the classifier recognises, with the Wikidata class it matches (labels checked against Wikidata, 2026-11-23) and the evidence the classifier reads for it. UNESCO's Memory of the World register (Q16024238) is cited as a reference for which documents count as world heritage, but it is not evidence: it also lists archives about events (the Nanjing Massacre) and scripts. Facet values have no ids field, so the ids live here, not in the timelines.

scripture.name: Scripture or religious text
scripture.evidence: titles (Vedas, Bible, Qur'an, Torah, Tripitaka, Avesta, Guru Granth Sahib…); infobox 'religious text'; categories 'religious texts', 'scriptures', 'sacred texts'

law-code.name: Law code
law-code.evidence: titles ('Code of …', 'Laws of …', Corpus Juris, Arthashastra, Manusmriti); categories 'law codes', 'legal codes'

charter.name: Charter, constitution or declaration
charter.evidence: titles (Magna Carta, 'Charter of …', 'Constitution of …', 'Declaration of Independence', 'Declaration of the Rights'); category 'charters'. A text that makes a state or declares independence keeps that act as its main category, with Foundational text second; a plain treaty stays Treaty.

epic-or-classic.name: Epic or classic
epic-or-classic.evidence: titles (Gilgamesh, Mahabharata, Iliad, Shahnameh, Analects, Kojiki, Popol Vuh…); infoboxes 'book', 'poem', 'literary work', 'written work'; categories 'epic poems', 'Chinese classic texts'

not_evidence.infobox document: policy letters and declarations (the Balfour Declaration) use it: stays Laws
not_evidence.infobox manuscript: records and surveys (Domesday Book) use it
not_evidence.Memory of the World Register: lists event archives and scripts too
